holidays.name: World Backup Day
holidays.description: A day for backing up your photos, documents and other digital files before disaster strikes. Back up your phone, copy your laptop to an external drive, and test that your backups actually restore. Your future self will be grateful.
holidays.origin: It began in the early 2010s, when tech enthusiasts in an online community proposed a day to remind people to protect their data. It has since spread across the tech industry and is observed worldwide each March 31.
holidays.funFact: The date was picked on purpose. It sits right before April Fools' Day, so nobody has to learn the hard way that losing all their files is no joke.

holidays.name: Dance Marathon Day
holidays.description: A day to lace up your dancing shoes and move for as long as your feet allow. Host a living-room dance-off, challenge friends to a boogie-athon, or just keep the playlist going well past your usual bedtime.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It nods to the dance marathon craze of the 1920s and 1930s, when couples shuffled for hours or even days to win prizes.
holidays.funFact: At the height of the 1930s craze, some contests ran for weeks. Some lasted for months, with contestants allowed short breaks each hour and even sleeping on their partner's shoulder while shuffling along.
